deities: Lord Krishna (worshipped through Guru Asanas of Srimanta Sankardev, Madhabdev and Padma Ata; no idol in the Kirtan Ghar)

history.period: Established 1583 AD (1505 Saka); present concrete structure 1878 (some sources say 1870 - conflict)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE IN THE CONVENTIONAL SENSE - a Vaishnavite satra (monastic prayer complex) and the dominant centre of Ekasarana Dharma in western Assam; keep-or-drop decision needed. Founded by the Vaishnavite saint Madhabdev in 1583 AD (earlier called Barpeta Than); he stayed eight years and entrusted it to his disciple Sri Mathuradasa (Mathura Das Burha) Ata, its first Satradhikar, who systematised its democratic administration - a system still in force. The Kirtan Ghar prayer hall at its centre has no idol of any god or goddess; three Guru Asanas dedicated to Krishna in composite form carry the lamp Akhay Banti, with a Bhaj Ghar (treasury), Math, Khatkhati canal ghat and a seven-stair Doul structure in the complex. Originally a kutcha house, it was rebuilt in concrete with big pillars and decorative wall paintings in 1878 (one source says 1870 - conflict flagged). Coordinates are Barpeta town-center level (the Satra stands centrally in the town; approximate - verify).

name: Barpeta Satra (Kirtan Ghar)
town_description: Barpeta is a town in western Assam about 95 km from Guwahati, often called the land of sattras. It is the cultural heart of the Neo-Vaishnavite movement founded by Srimanta Sankardev and Madhabdev, known for its sattras, the annual Raas and Doul festivals, and its handloom and brass craft traditions.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati - about 95 km by road
travel.railway: Barpeta Road railway station (nearest); rail route via Katihar and Siliguri
travel.road: Well connected by road from Guwahati (95 km); auto rickshaws/taxis reach the Satra gate, beyond which no vehicles are allowed

visitor_information.best_time: Throughout the year; Raas Mahotsava (Oct-Nov) and Doul Utsav (Feb-Mar) are the major festival seasons
